$comment: Findings that have been assessed and are not being fixed yet, and why.
This is not a suppression list. tools/dependency_scan.py prints every entry
on every run under 'accepted', so an exception stays visible for as long as
it exists; what it changes is whether the build fails, not whether anyone is
told. An entry without a 'review_by' date, or one whose date has passed, is
reported as EXPIRED and stops excusing anything - so an exception that is
never revisited turns back into a failure rather than quietly becoming
An entry belongs here only when the finding has been traced to actual code
and the fix has a cost worth naming. 'We do not think it applies' is not a
reason; 'this is the call site, and here is why it cannot be reached' is.
Where a patch release fixes it, the patch release is taken instead - see the

accepted.because: Open redirect via a backslash in <Link> and useNavigate. It requires the application to route to a target it did not construct, and this one never does: there is no next/redirect/returnTo parameter anywhere in the frontend, and every dynamic destination is built by a helper that emits a rooted internal path with encodeURIComponent on each variable segment. The advisory's other half, arbitrary constructor injection through deserializeErrors(), is in the server-side rendering hydration path, and this frontend is a static bundle with no SSR at all. The only published fix is react-router-dom 7.18.3, a major version whose routing API differs from the 6.x this application is written against - that is a frontend migration, not a dependency bump, and doing it inside a security window would mean changing every route to close a path that cannot be reached.
accepted.review_because: Revisit when the frontend is next touched, or sooner if a 6.x patch appears. Re-check first whether any redirect-target parameter has been introduced, because that is the assumption this rests on.
